question: Hair with no pigment is made of translucent keratin, so why does it look white rather than clear?
answer: Because it scatters light. A hair is full of internal boundaries, between cells and fibres and around air pockets in its core, and each reflects a little light of every colour. Many small reflections of all colours add up to white, as in snow. Grey is white hairs among dark ones.
move: Many clear surfaces together can make something opaque.
ask: What looks like one solid thing to me but is really many clear things stacked up?
source: Robbins, Chemical and Physical Behavior of Human Hair
reference: Robbins, Chemical and Physical Behavior of Human Hair, 5th edition, Springer, 2012
